summary: The paper investigates representation grafting between a 7B donor specialist and a frozen 14B host model on a 512-triplet Python repair task. It demonstrates that replacing dynamic per-prompt donor activations with a static 32-dimensional calibration mean vector improves task performance from 166 to 232 solved groups while eliminating 7B inference costs. The evaluation includes strong negative controls and exact hardware/runtime receipts.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including zero donor ablation, matched host-feature bridge, shuffled targets, and cyclic feature exchange within triplets.

Clear practical payoff: replacing dynamic donor passes with a single pre-calculated constant vector yields an absolute gain of 12.89 percentage points over early exit maps while eliminating donor runtime overhead.
High mathematical and reporting consistency; percentage gains, confidence intervals (+8.40 to +17.58), and net group tallies (+106 / -40) are internally consistent and mathematically exact.
Comprehensive reproducibility metadata detailing OS build, package versions (MLX, MLX-LM, NumPy), peak memory, and verification script hashes.
weaknesses: Evaluation is confined to a single task (Python bracket repair triplets) and single model pair (Qwen2.5-7B donor into Qwen2.5-14B host), limiting generalizability across diverse coding benchmarks and architectures.

Mechanistic explanation is minimal; the article observes that the static calibration mean acts as a task-conditioned steering signal but does not investigate why dynamic donor activations underperform or introduce variance.
The submission was provided without an attached repository object in platform metadata, requiring a text-only evaluation badge.
suggestions: Extend the evaluation to broader standard coding benchmarks (e.g., HumanEval, MBPP, or SWE-bench Lite) to verify whether static steering vectors consistently beat dynamic donor representations.

Perform a geometric and cosine similarity analysis comparing prompt-specific donor vectors to the calibration mean to identify why dynamic residual perturbations degrade accuracy relative to the fixed centroid.
Test sensitivity to calibration sample size (varying the 192 calibration triplets) to determine how many examples are necessary to compute an effective fixed steering vector.

claims.text: The 14B recipient with the same 32-value vector on every prompt solved 232 of 512 complete Python repair groups.
Both the full donor and the prompt-dependent ten-block feature map scored 166.
The constant gained 12.89 percentage points over the early map (95% paired interval +8.40 to +17.58) and 32.03 points over the matched host-feature bridge.
The BF16 Qwen2.5-14B model ran on the Apple M5 Ultra with 256 GiB unified memory, macOS build 26B118, Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2, NumPy 2.5.5 and tokenizers 0.23.3.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Representation Engineering and Activation Steering in Large Language Models
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Demonstrates that in trained cross-model feature grafts, an invariant mean vector extracted from donor residuals functions as a superior task-level prior over dynamic per-token donor features.
